title: A degree-two criterion for continuous cohomology
statement: Let $G$ be profinite and $\ell$ prime. Suppose that $H^2(H,\mathbf F_\ell)=0$ for every open subgroup $H\subset G$, with trivial coefficients. Then $H^q(G,M)=0$ for $q\geq2$ and every discrete continuous $\ell$-primary module $M$, with cohomology as in [def-exc-continuous-cohomology].

proof.text: Let $M$ be finite. By [lem-sc-sylow-module-filtration], choose an open $H\subseteq G$ of index prime to $\ell$ such that $M|_H$ has a finite filtration with trivial $\mathbf F_\ell$ successive quotients. The hypothesis gives $H^2(H,\mathbf F_\ell)=0$; the long exact sequences for the filtration, inducting on its length, therefore give $H^2(H,M)=0$. Apply [lem-sc-group-h2-transfer] to this $H$ and $M$: restriction followed by corestriction is multiplication by $[G:H]$, and that integer is invertible on the $\ell$-primary group $H^2(G,M)$. Thus $H^2(G,M)=0$.
For arbitrary $M$, use [lem-sc-group-cohomology-filtered-union]. Every finite submodule in that directed system satisfies $H^2(G,M_i)=0$ by Step 1, so the colimit comparison gives $H^2(G,M)=0$.

For every $M$, [lem-sc-group-coinduced-acyclic] supplies an equivariant embedding $M\hookrightarrow I=\operatorname{Cont}(G,M)$, with $I$ discrete and $\ell$-primary and $H^q(G,I)=0$ for $q\geq1$. Let $Q=I/M$; it is again discrete and $\ell$-primary. The long exact sequence for $0\to M\to I\to Q\to0$ gives $H^{q+1}(G,M)\cong H^q(G,Q)$ for every $q\geq1$. Iterating this dimension shift reduces each degree $r\geq2$ to $H^2(G,Q')$ for a discrete $\ell$-primary module $Q'$, which vanishes by Steps 1 and 2.
